rule_message.title: Balanced Throughput
rule_message.message: Compute and Memory are well-balanced: To reduce runtime, both computation and memory traffic must be reduced. Check both the @section:ComputeWorkloadAnalysis:Compute Workload Analysis@ and @section:MemoryWorkloadAnalysis:Memory Workload Analysis@ sections.

Every scheduler is capable of issuing one instruction per cycle, but for this workload each scheduler only issues an instruction every 5.6 cycles. This might leave hardware resources underutilized and may lead to less optimal performance. Out of the maximum of 12 warps per scheduler, this workload allocates an average of 2.47 active warps per scheduler, but only an average of 0.22 warps were eligible per cycle. Eligible warps are the subset of active warps that are ready to issue their next instruction. Every cycle with no eligible warp results in no instruction being issued and the issue slot remains unused. To increase the number of eligible warps, avoid possible load imbalances due to highly different execution durations per warp. Reducing stalls indicated on the @section:WarpStateStats:Warp State Statistics@ and @section:SourceCounters:Source Counters@ sections can help, too.

focus_metrics.name: smsp__issue_active.avg.per_cycle_active
focus_metrics.info: Increase the average number of instructions issued per cycle

rule_message.title: Wait Stalls
rule_message.message: On average, each warp of this workload spends 4.5 cycles being stalled waiting on a fixed latency execution dependency. Typically, this stall reason should be very low and only shows up as a top contributor in already highly optimized kernels. Try to hide the corresponding instruction latencies by increasing the number of active warps, restructuring the code or unrolling loops. Furthermore, consider switching to lower-latency instructions, e.g. by making use of fast math compiler options. For example, FFMA-to-FFMA dependency latency is 4 cycles. This stall type represents about 32.6% of the total average of 13.8 cycles between issuing two instructions.

focus_metrics.name: smsp__issue_active.avg.per_cycle_active
focus_metrics.info: Increase the average number of instructions issued per cycle

focus_metrics.name: smsp_average_wait
focus_metrics.info: Decrease the number of cycles spent in wait stalls

rule_message.message: Check the @section:SourceCounters:Warp Stall Sampling (All Samples)@ table for the top stall locations in your source based on sampling data. The @url:Profiling Guide:https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#metrics-reference@ provides more details on each stall reason.

rule_message.title: High Utilization
rule_message.message: Tensor is the highest-utilized pipeline (60.4%) based on elapsed cycles in the workload, taking into account the rates of its different instructions. It is the logical aggregation of individual tensor pipelines. It's dominated by its Tensor (FP) sub-pipeline. The pipeline is well-utilized, but might become a bottleneck if more work is added. Based on the number of executed instructions, the highest utilized pipeline (60.4%) is Tensor (FP). It executes 16-bit floating point tensor operations. Comparing the two, the overall pipeline utilization appears to be caused by frequent, low-latency instructions. See the @url:Profiling Guide:https://docs.nvidia.com/nsight-compute/ProfilingGuide/index.html#metrics-decoder@ or hover over the pipeline name to understand the workloads handled by each pipeline. The @section:InstructionStats:Instruction Statistics@ section shows the mix of executed instructions for this workload. Check the @section:WarpStateStats:Warp State Statistics@ section for which reasons cause warps to stall.

focus_metrics.name: sm__pipe_tensor_cycles_active.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed
focus_metrics.info: Try to decrease the utilization of the busiest pipeline (currently: Tensor)

result_tables.title: Most frequently executed instructions for pipeline Tensor
result_tables.description: Source lines with the highest number of executed instructions on pipeline Tensor (FP).

rule_message.title: L1TEX Global Load Access Pattern
rule_message.message: The memory access pattern for global loads from L1TEX might not be optimal. On average, only 31.9 of the 32 bytes transmitted per sector are utilized by each thread. This could possibly be caused by a stride between threads. Check the @section:SourceCounters:Source Counters@ section for uncoalesced global loads.

focus_metrics.info: Increase the average number of bytes utilized per sector towards 32 bytes

focus_metrics.name: l1tex__throughput.avg.pct_of_peak_sustained_elapsed
focus_metrics.info: The higher the L1TEX throughput the more severe the issue becomes

rule_message.title: L2 Global Store Access Pattern
rule_message.message: The memory access pattern for global stores to L2 might not be optimal. On average, only 31.9 of the 32 bytes transmitted per sector are utilized by each thread. This applies to the 100.0% of sectors missed in L1TEX. This could possibly be caused by a stride between threads. Check the @section:SourceCounters:Source Counters@ section for uncoalesced global stores.
